summary: A camp from 1916 that became an L-4 cab, now not in use and reached on foot past a forest-road closure that began in 2014.

facts.design: L-4 ground cab on a cement foundation, after an earlier log cupola cabin
facts.status_note: Structure still on the summit but not in use

access.note: Forest road FS-478 under a temporary closure that began in 2014 and appeared still in place at the August 2020 guide update. Hike-in only.

visit.trail_note: Per the 2020 climbing guide: from the Rice Lake trailhead, the summit is 1.0 mile up the Rice Peak Trail. The Boise NF slide show describes a start where the road washes out and a hike of 4.25 miles each way.

Log cupola cabin, the first structure built on the site
Present L-4 ground cab on a cement foundation. The Boise NF slide show heading says 1937 and a Forest Lookouts page gives only 193?; see notes

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register titles it Rice Peak (Blue Point) Lookout. The Boise NF slide show says Blue Point Lookout was later renamed Rice Peak Lookout, so both names refer to one tower.
The 1916 camp and the 1922 log cupola cabin were earlier structures on the site. The 1940 L-4 cab is the present one.

notes_for_editor: Build date is not settled. 1940 (register, Idaho Fire Lookouts, firelookout.com) vs 1937 (Boise NF slide show heading 'Blue Point Lookout, 1937') vs 193? (Forest Lookouts). Staffing: no source gives a staffing history, so no staffing fact is recorded. The FS-478 closure status comes from an August 2020 guide; no Forest Service order or current page was read, so verify before publishing. The slide show and the climbing guide describe different routes; the story reports both. Elevation 8,696 ft (2,651 m) matches the record's 2650.5 m.
